html:
The Cupeño are a Native people of Southern California, whose home was a small valley at the hot springs of Kupa, now Warner Springs, in the mountains of San Diego County. Their language is Uto-Aztecan, close to that of the Cahuilla.

Their land later became part of Warner's Ranch. After a long court fight the US Supreme Court ruled for the ranch owners in 1901, and in 1903 the Cupeño were evicted and moved to the Pala Reservation, a forced march they remember as their own trail of tears. Their descendants live at Pala alongside the Luiseño, and among the Kumeyaay and Cahuilla bands nearby.
